Noise
The Milwaukee County Expressway and Transportation Commission engaged a consultant to analyze the noise impact for the approved Airport Spur design alignment within Corridor #5. A noise analysis was not undertaken for the other corridors because both the type and magnitude of noise impacts would be similar to those of the design alignment within Corridor #5.
The noise study was performed in accordance with the Federal Highway Administration's Policy and Procedure Memorandum (PPM) 90-2 identified as "Noise Standards and Procedures", dated February 8, 1973. The relationship between these federal noise standards and existing land use is shown in figure 18. The noise impact was determined by taking field measurements of existing noise levels and comparing these levels with 1990 predicted noise levels.
The study area is bounded on the west by 20th Street, on the east by Howell Avenue, and on the north and south by Grange and Ramsey Avenues respectively. The existing land uses are residential, industrial, and commercial. There is one school, the Hamlin Garland School located on Goldcrest Avenue. The study area is presently subjected to noise from existing I-94, General Mitchell Field, as well as local street traffic.
Field noise measurements were obtained from July 10, 1972 through August 22, 1972. Noise levels for the year 1990 were predicted using the Federal Highway Administration's highway noise prediction computer program.
